tests_run: text-contrast (computed from dom-1920 colours, sweep could not verify)

findings.where: subtitle, metric categories, comparison labels, source note, footer insight, wordmark
findings.evidence: Sweep contrast was not verified (no background render). Computed from dom-1920 against #fafaf8: subtitle rgb(160,160,154) 14px = 2.52:1; "Mathematical Reasoning" rgb(184,180,174) 11px = 1.97:1; model labels "GLM-4.7" rgb(168,164,160) 11px = 2.37:1; values "88.2" #999 = 2.73:1; footer insight body #999 13px = 2.73:1; "Benchmark Evaluation 2025 Official Results" rgb(192,188,182) 10px = 1.81:1; "ZHIPU AI" rgb(200,196,188) = 1.66:1.
findings.before: Grey ramp from #999 to #c8c4bc for all supporting text
findings.after: Supporting text at #595959 or darker (7:1 on #fafaf8 for projection); labels at #6b6b6b minimum (4.5:1)
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum): every text run except the title and figures is below 4.5:1, most below 3:1; projection lowers contrast further.

findings.where: accented GLM-4.7 values "95.7", "73.8%", "87.4" in the comparison rows
findings.evidence: The winning value and bar are marked only by terracotta rgb(212,165,116), 2.13:1 against the ground, so the highlighted values are also the least legible text in each row.
findings.after: .comp-val.gold { color: #8a5a2b; font-weight: 600 } (about 5:1, plus weight as a second cue)
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.3 Contrast and 1.4.1 Use of Color: the emphasis channel fails contrast and relies on hue.

findings.where: comparison bars for Claude 3.5 and GPT-4o
findings.evidence: Comparator bars are thin light-grey lines on a near-white track (visible in 1920-00 at y 653 and 675), well under 3:1 against the track; the bar length is the data.
findings.before: Light grey 2px bars on a pale track
findings.after: Bars at #767676 or darker, 4px+ thick, with the track removed or lightened
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast: graphical objects that carry data need 3:1.

findings.evidence: dom-1920 text for the first figure is "957" with the decimal point in a separate decorative span; if the dot span is hidden or styled as a glyph, the value is extracted as 957, not 95.7.
findings.after: Keep the real '.' character in the figure's text and colour it via a span that stays in the text flow, or add aria-label="95.7" on the figure
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships: copied or exported text must keep the value.

findings.evidence: dom-1920: no heading elements; the title "Coding Capability Breakthrough." is div.main-title and metric names are divs; no landmarks.
findings.after: <h1 class="main-title"> and <h2> for each benchmark name, so PDF export tags and screen readers get an outline
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships; matters once the slide is exported to tagged PDF (SLD-105).

strengths: Title and the three figures are near-black on off-white (13.7:1) and very large.
Every comparison row has a text label and a numeric value, so the bars are not the only carrier of the data.
not_investigated: Keyboard, focus and target checks skipped: fixed-canvas slide with no interactive elements (sweep disabled them by profile).
Sweep text_floor hits (10-14px on a 1920 slide) checked against the tile: real, not disputed.
Projection or PDF export not tested.
